violations.description: A hardcoded Stripe API key sits in tracked source.
violations.evidence: config.py:2 STRIPE_KEY is set to a non-placeholder Stripe key (len 32, entropy 4.7) and imported by app.py:3.
violations.recommendation: Rotate the key now, load it from an environment variable or a secret manager, and purge it from git history.

violations.description: A .env file holding an AWS access key ID and a DB password is committed.
violations.evidence: .env:1 AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID (real-looking, not a placeholder) and .env:2 DB_PASSWORD were added in commit 43cf215.
violations.recommendation: Rotate the AWS credentials and DB password, git rm --cached .env, add .env to .gitignore, provide a .env.example, and purge it from history.

violations.description: The repository has no automated tests.
violations.evidence: The tracked files contain no tests/ directory and no test_*.py files. Only app.py, config.py and utils.py hold code.
violations.recommendation: Add pytest tests for the Flask route (using the test client with a mocked requests call) and for utils.load.

violations.description: There is no continuous integration configuration.
violations.evidence: inspect_ci found 0 workflow files and no other CI config.
violations.recommendation: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on push and pull_request to main, installs dependencies, lints and runs tests.

violations.description: A bare except silently swallows every error in the request handler.
violations.evidence: app.py:13-14 'except: pass', so the view returns None (an HTTP 500) with no logging.
violations.recommendation: Catch requests.RequestException specifically, log it, and return a proper error response.

violations.description: The app hardcodes a data file path under a developer's home directory.
violations.recommendation: Read DATA_FILE from an environment variable, or use a path relative to the project.

violations.description: utils.load reads from a hardcoded Windows user Desktop path.
violations.recommendation: Take the path as a parameter or read it from an environment variable or config.

violations.description: The production database host is hardcoded in the single config module.
violations.evidence: config.py:3 DB_HOST = 'prod-db.internal.example.com'. No environment-based override exists.
violations.recommendation: Read DB_HOST from an environment variable so each environment can set its own value.

violations.description: The application's runtime dependencies have no version constraints.
violations.evidence: requirements.txt lists flask (L1) and requests (L2) with no version specifiers, and there is no lockfile.
violations.recommendation: Pin exact versions (e.g. flask==3.x.y), or use pip-tools to generate a pinned lock.

violations.description: There is no README at the repository root.
violations.evidence: None of the 8 tracked files is a README.
violations.recommendation: Add a README.md covering purpose, setup, required environment variables and how to run the app.

violations.evidence: list_files shows no .gitignore. As a result, .env, __pycache__/, server.log and .DS_Store are all tracked.
violations.recommendation: Add a Python .gitignore that covers __pycache__/, *.pyc, .env, *.log, .DS_Store and .venv/.

violations.description: The main entrypoint runs Flask in debug mode bound to all interfaces.
violations.evidence: app.py:17 app.run(host='0.0.0.0', debug=True). Debug mode exposes the Werkzeug interactive debugger on the network.
violations.recommendation: Control debug through an environment variable that defaults to False, and serve production traffic with a WSGI server such as gunicorn.

violations.description: TLS certificate verification is turned off for an outbound HTTPS request.
violations.evidence: app.py:11 requests.get('https://api.example.com', verify=False) in the request handler.
violations.recommendation: Remove verify=False. If a custom CA is needed, pass verify=<ca_bundle_path>.

violations.description: No linter or formatter is configured or enforced.
violations.evidence: The repo has no pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, pre-commit config or CI lint step.
violations.recommendation: Configure ruff (in pyproject.toml or pre-commit) and run it in CI.

violations.description: A macOS metadata file is committed.
violations.evidence: .DS_Store is tracked at the repo root.

violations.description: A runtime log file is committed.
violations.recommendation: Remove it from tracking and add *.log to .gitignore.
